- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in adjusting to new equilibrium.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high forecasts longer than observed price behavior suggests.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model lacks downward pressure modeling or ignores policy/seasonal adjustments.
- Model underreacts to recent low prices — fails to recognize when prices are “too high” and adjusts downward.
- When true price is below historical mean, model still forecasts above mean — exhibits anchoring bias.
- Model often fails to capture short-term volatility spikes — underestimates or misplaces timing of price corrections.
- Forecasting for 30d horizon tends to be overly optimistic — especially when recent history shows downward trend or policy tightening.
